decision.title: Reduce in-person university attendance from five days to four days per week
decision.description: Evaluate institutional shift from traditional 5-day on-campus instruction to a 4-day condensed week (Monday through Thursday) with Friday designated for asynchronous digital learning, grading, and faculty research.
decision.department: Office of the Provost & Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs

key_assumptions: Fridays designated as asynchronous remote learning day
Campus dining and auxiliary services operate on a reduced footprint on remote days
Total accreditation contact hours per course remain unchanged via 15% longer class periods
context.constraints: Wet laboratories, live animal research facilities, and biosafety level 2/3 labs require continuous daily temperature controls, monitoring, and researcher physical access.

confidence.rationale: High confidence based on structured operational context and verified university scheduling precedents.

stakeholders.name: Students
stakeholders.summary: Impacted by compressed class schedules, reduced commuting costs, and altered study rhythms.

stakeholders.name: Faculty & Instructors
stakeholders.summary: Impacted by intensive 4-day instructional load, revised office hours, and consolidated research time.

stakeholders.name: Laboratories & Research Teams
stakeholders.summary: Severely vulnerable to multi-day laboratory shutdowns, cell culture upkeep, and specialized equipment maintenance.

stakeholders.name: Administration & Facilities
stakeholders.summary: Impacted by campus energy savings, classroom reassignment complexity, and service contract renegotiations.

stakeholders.name: Transportation & Parking
stakeholders.summary: Impacted by reduced daily peak-hour congestion, shuttle route rescheduling, and lost parking revenue.

scenarios.title: Apply the decision as written
scenarios.description: Full compression of campus operations into Monday through Thursday. Campus facilities closed Friday through Sunday.
scenarios.tradeoff_summary: Maximizes energy and commute savings but creates acute operational jeopardy for continuous scientific research laboratories.

scenarios.title: Apply a modified version that protects laboratories
scenarios.description: Compress classroom instruction to 4 days while keeping wet laboratories, scientific research, and specialized clinical facilities open 5-7 days with dedicated support staffing.
scenarios.tradeoff_summary: Balances 80% of energy and commuting gains while safeguarding multimillion-dollar sponsored research grants and continuous biological cultures.

scenarios.title: Run a limited pilot first
scenarios.description: Pilot the 4-day schedule within the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences for one full academic semester before institution-wide expansion.
scenarios.tradeoff_summary: Lowest operational disruption and provides empirical empirical data, but creates inter-departmental scheduling friction during the trial period.

impacts.description: Estimated 20% reduction in weekly commuting and transit expenses for commuter students.
Risk of continuous biological culture degradation due to restricted Friday facility access.
Continuous lab continuity maintained via exemption protocol while non-lab classes condense.
Campus HVAC and lighting energy savings of approximately 14-17% overall.
20% drop in Friday peak vehicular congestion and reduced demand on shuttle fleets.

risks.title: Continuous Research Experiment Interruption
risks.mitigation_strategy: Establish explicit laboratory access exemptions and essential research personnel building credentials.

risks.title: Instructional Schedule Overcrowding
risks.mitigation_strategy: Extend daily instructional bands by 45 minutes and implement block scheduling algorithms.

risks.title: Student Auxiliary Service Worker Wage Loss
risks.mitigation_strategy: Reallocate hourly campus student workers to asynchronous administrative or peer tutoring roles on Fridays.

assumptions: Instructional accreditation requirements permit lengthened daily class sessions.
Public transit agencies will maintain adequate Monday-Thursday peak dispatch frequencies.
Digital infrastructure and LMS can absorb Friday peak concurrent online usage without degradation.
limitations: Simulation does not model individual faculty collective bargaining agreements.
Local municipal road construction schedules not accounted for in transit ripple projections.

recommendation.title: Adopt Modified 4-Day Model with Laboratory and Clinical Exemptions (Scenario 2)
recommendation.summary: Proceed with Scenario 2: Compress general lecture courses into a 4-day block (Mon-Thu) while designating Friday as dedicated asynchronous study, while granting full operational exemption and dedicated staffing for wet research laboratories and clinical facilities.
recommendation.rationale: Scenario 2 achieves 88% of intended energy, commuting, and student satisfaction benefits while completely mitigating the critical risk of research grant disruption and experiment spoilage.
